([[Branson, Missouri]]) | college = *[[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] (2022–present) | highlights = * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2022]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2022) }} '''Jordan Walsh''' (born March 3, 2004) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]] of the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC). ==Early life and high school== Walsh grew up in [[Desoto, Texas]] and initially attended Faith Family Academy in [[Dallas, Texas]]. He averaged 18 points, 11 rebounds, five assists, 2.4 steals and 2.3 blocks per game and was named class 4A All-State as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2021/09/24/memphis-basketball-recruiting-5-star-jordan-walsh-official-visit-penny-hardaway-larry-brown/5834067001/|title=Memphis basketball recruiting: 5-star Jordan Walsh taking official visit|work=[[The Commercial Appeal]]|date=September 24, 2021|access-date=January 22, 2023}} Walsh transferred to Link Academy in [[Branson, Missouri]] prior to the start of his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2021/09/06/four-star-basketball-recruit-jordan-walsh-leaves-faith-family-now-at-prep-academy-in-missouri/|title=Four-star basketball recruit Jordan Walsh leaves Faith Family, now at prep academy in Missouri|work=[[Dallas Morning News]]|date=September 6, 2021|access-date=January 22, 2023}} He averaged 15.3 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 3.1 assists in his only season at Link.{{cite web|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/p0UAhQj8q0iWR3GgkizMKg/high-school-basketball-maxpreps-player-of-the-year-in-all-50-states.htm|title=High school basketball: MaxPreps Player of the Year in all 50 states|first=Jordan|last=Divens|website=[[MaxPreps.com]]|date=March 24, 2022|access-date=February 5, 2023}} Walsh was selected to play in the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.fox16.com/sports/local-sports/nick-smith-jr-jordan-walsh-named-mcdonalds-all-americans/|title=Nick Smith Jr & Jordan Walsh named McDonald’s All-Americans|first=Alyssa|last=Orange|website=[[KLRT-TV|FOX16.com]]|date=January 25, 2022|access-date=January 22, 2023}} Walsh was rated a five-star recruit.{{cite web|url=https://arkansas.rivals.com/news/walsh-shows-potential-in-win-over-oklahoma|title=Walsh shows potential in win over Oklahoma|first=Mason|last=Choate|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=December 11, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/arkansas-basketball-recruiting-five-star-sf-jordan-walsh-commits-to-razorbacks/|title=Arkansas basketball recruiting: Five-star SF Jordan Walsh commits to Razorbacks|first=Kyle|last=Boone|website=[[CBS Sports]]|date=October 14, 2021|access-date=February 10, 2023}} [[ESPN]] analyst Paul Biancardi rated him as the best two-way player in the 2023 recruiting class.{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/may/23/espns-paul-biancardi-names-hog-signee-top-two-way-player/|title=ESPN's Biancardi names Hog signee top 2-way player|work=[[The Arkansas web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32401700/jordan-walsh-ranked-no-7-2022-class-announces-commitment-arkansas|title=Jordan Walsh, ranked No. 7 in the 2022 class, announces commitment to Arkansas|first1=Jeff|last1=Borzello|first2=Paul|last2=Biancardi|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=October 14, 2021|access-date=January 22, 2023}} ==College career== Walsh entered his freshman season at Arkansas as starting [[Wing (basketball)|wing]].{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2023/jan/22/hogs-find-their-d-vs-rebels/|title=Hogs find their 'D' vs. Rebels|work=[[The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=January 22, 2023|access-date=January 30, 2023}} Midway through the season he was moved to the bench as a key reserve.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/arkansas/hogs-mens-basketball/razorbacks-walsh-sec-mitchell-texas-aggies-south-carolina-gamecocks-fouls-accident-musselman|title=Musselman's Unplanned Handling of Walsh Against A&M Unlocks Key to Future Wins|first=Kent|last=Smith|website=[[SI.com]]|date=February 1, 2023|access-date=February 6, 2023}} ==Personal life== Walsh has [[alopecia]], an autoimmune condition which prevents the growth of hair on the body.{{cite web|url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/dfwvarsity/article227461714.html|title=Faith Family freshman, who won state on
